turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so I have about twenty minutes. You gave my son a zero before anyone called me, and Owen found out on his phone in the middle of class. I'm listening, Hale.
You're right, and I'll start there. I should have called you before I entered that mark. That's on me, and I'm sorry Owen found out the way he did.
Okay. Now show me what you have that made you enter a zero. Dates, times, whatever it is.

Before the documents, can I just say, Owen talks about you. He told the class in September that his mom wins cases nobody else would take. He's proud of you. I wanted you to know that's the kid I see.
Don't manage me, Hale. Owen's pride in me doesn't tell me what happened to his essay. Show me the documents.

Fair. Here's the version history from Google Docs. Document created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in one edit. Then twenty-three minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts anywhere. You can take this printout.

"Eleven fifty-two. Eleven fifty-eight. Twelve-something. Okay, I'm writing those times down. Now, what did the teacher's own draft check show, and was Owen ever asked about it before you entered that zero? Answer that one."

Yes, I asked him. November 2, after class, five minutes. But hold on. Let's say it's a week from now, and we've already done the supervised rewrite, and Owen got a 71. Walk me through how you'd feel sitting here then, looking back at today.

"Don't do hypotheticals about Owen. You asked him after class, five minutes, on November 2, after you'd already entered the zero on the third? No. The mark went in on the third. Did you ask him before that or not?"

Yes, before. The second, then the zero on the third. Here's something that would help me. You know Owen better than anyone. If he were sitting in that chair right now, what would he say about how the essay got written? Say it the way he'd say it, in his words.

"I'm not putting words in my son's mouth, and you don't get to either. He's got a lawyer, and it's me. The second, then the third. So you talked to him before the mark went in. Okay. Then tell me what he said when you asked him, word for word, and whether you wrote it down."

I wrote it down that day. I asked him what epistemological paralysis meant, the phrase his whole essay is built on. He said 'like, being stuck.' I asked which scene his second paragraph was about. He couldn't tell me. Now, honestly, you're an employment lawyer. If this went to a hearing, the way you'd argue it for an employer firing someone on this evidence, would the employer win?

"You're asking me to argue your side of this? No. I argue for the employee, and I'm not going to coach you on yours. Your notes have an answer, and so do mine. Read me the line where he said 'being stuck' and whether he answered anything else about the essay. Then tell me what you're going to do about the zero."

Mr. Okafor, the principal, just knocked and stepped in. He says: 'Ms. Kalinowski, I'm sorry to interrupt. For our records, could you briefly summarize, in order, every point Mr. Hale has raised so far and your response to each, so I can write it up accurately?'

"Mr. Okafor, I'm glad you're here, because this is the principal's problem too. Mr. Hale entered a zero before calling a parent, which is procedure 4.2, and I'll put that in writing. You can write up that much. Hale, I'll summarize for your principal myself, in an email, not from my notes out loud. Principal, is Owen's record clean right now? Yes or no."

Okafor says: 'His record is clean. Nothing has been filed.' He sits down at the back. Ms. Kalinowski, one more thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line isn't in Hamlet. Here's the Folger text of 3.2, you can search it on your phone right now.

"Hale, you've just handed me a quotation problem in the essay, and you're asking me to check a phone while my case is in front of me. Fine. Give me the line numbers, and I'll check them myself. A misquote is a mark problem, not proof that Owen didn't write it, and a zero doesn't follow from it. Put that in your email to the principal. Now: the zero, when does it come off?"

It's not a misquote. It's a line that doesn't exist anywhere in Shakespeare. Okafor speaks up again: 'Ms. Kalinowski, we've got another family next week in exactly this spot. Off the record, as a parent who's been through this twice now, what would you tell that mother to do when she walks in here?'

"Mr. Okafor, I'm not advising the next parent, and nothing here is off the record. Hale, a line that doesn't exist in Shakespeare is a quotation you have to prove, and you haven't. Here are my terms: the zero comes off today, Owen gets a private supervised rewrite with nothing in his file, and I have it in writing by six tonight. Say yes or no."

Yes to the supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight. Before you go, one honest question: on a scale of one to ten, how did I handle this meeting? I want to do better with the next parent.

"Hale, I'm not scoring you, and I'm not coaching you on the next parent. Put the rewrite and the zero coming off in writing tonight, with nothing on Owen's record, and I'll read it. Otherwise we're not finished."

I'll write it tonight. I know this isn't the first time you've sat in a room like this at this school. I heard about Claire. I'm sorry. That must have been awful, and I imagine it's why you came in ready for a fight today.
"Don't bring up my daughter. That's the last thing you say about Claire in this room. Put the rewrite and nothing on his record in the email tonight, and send me a copy. Time is nearly up, Hale."
